From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>

Subject: Capacity runbook & unit-econ — QBR readiness check (actionable asks)

Team —

We have one week until the QBR slot with leadership. Need a concise runbook and the delta to unit economics if we pull any of the following levers for the next quarter: reserved slots, aggressive batching, prefix/KV caching at 30/60/90% hit rates, and short-form quantized variants for tail traffic. Please treat this as an "ask list + evidence" item — we want a single slide and a one-page appendix that leadership can read before the meeting.

Deliverables and owners (deadline: 2026-07-02 EOD PT):
- Capacity heatmap + runway: actualized by Marissa (include burst assumptions and lead times; show 95th percentile utilization)
- Unit-econ sensitivity table: Marissa + Karthik (show $/token delta by slot type, batching, and cache hit scenarios)
- Tactical runbook (what to throttle/route/evict): Karthik (include fallback policies and opt-in thresholds)
- Talking notes and one-paragraph executive summary: Lauren (I can draft if you want)

Attached I put my quick sketch (unit-econ-deltas.xlsx) and a rough heatmap export (capacity-heatmap.png). Also cc'd Nimbus to confirm lead times on any additional reserved capacity.

Key constraints to call out up front:
- If we assume 80% average slot utilization, the marginal $/token is still highly sensitive to batching and cache; leadership will want a clear tradeoff.
- For enterprise customers (e.g., FjordHealth) we should show a sample SLA-tailored plan — they are on the agenda for expansion asks.

High-level ask: prioritize a single recommended configuration (color-coded green/yellow/red) for 1) cost-min, 2) latency-SLO, 3) enterprise-isolation.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Capacity runbook & unit-econ — QBR readiness check (actionable asks)

Thanks Mina — precise and high signal. A few priorities from my side:

1) Focus slides on two scenarios: conservative runway (no new reserved buys) and aggressive runway (reserve + cache opt-in). We don't need >2 scenarios.
2) For the QBR deck, leadership wants the marginal $/token at 95th pctl and a short statement of operational risk (one sentence).
3) If the recommended configuration increases latency beyond our SLO for tail customers, include a mitigator (e.g., fall back to hosted smaller model variant).

I will craft the one-paragraph exec summary after I see the numbers — call out which scenario minimizes spend vs preserves enterprise latency. If you want me to draft early, send the delta table and I'll iterate.

-Lauren

Uploading a short data dump and first-pass numbers. See attached: unit-econ-deltas.xlsx (tabs: baseline, reserve-buy, batching-sims, cache-hits) and capacity-heatmap.png. Quick notes:

- Baseline (current): 62% avg slot utilization; 95th pctl = 88% during peak windows (US-west)
- Reserve-buy scenario: committing to two additional p100 pools reduces marginal $/token by approx 14% at current traffic if we reach 75% utilization; lead time ~ 6 weeks (Nimbus confirms below)
- Batching sims: increasing batch target from 8->14 nets ~9% savings at similar latency median; tail p99 increase is non-linear and needs runbook mitigator
- Caching: a 60% KV/prefix hit rate reduces token spend by ~18% for chat workloads with warm sessions; cold-starts unchanged

Two asks for Karthik: please add a short table for the expected p99 delta for each batching/caching combo (we need that to justify fallbacks).

Marissa

Quick experiment notes and an inline excerpt for the runbook:

- Batching: We should treat target batch size as a knob by route; short-chat routes get target=10, long-form generation target=18. Expect median latency increase ~6-9% at those batch sizes, p99 delta depends on queueing policy.
- Cache eviction: Recommend TTL-based eviction per tenant with a soft-cap on KV store of 60% of memory; eviction reduces cold-start rate and preserves RPS headroom.
- Rollout plan: increment batch target in canary (5% traffic) -> 25% -> 60% -> full. At each step, measure p95/p99 and error rate. Rollback if p99 > SLO+40ms or error >0.5%.

I've added a p99 delta column to the sheet (link below). Also attached a draft PDF runbook for ops (batching-cache-runbook.pdf).

Link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1a2b3c-redwood-capacity-model (sheet: p99-deltas)

-Karthik
